Update the environment-signals blueprint's decision record for the follow-up that closed most of its recorded gaps: workspace locality now comes from the SSH address discovery reports (falling back to the provider's backend name only when there is no address), owed restarts are released one machine at a time, and the connectivity probe spends one budget per endpoint rather than per resolved address and checks the public internet hosts concurrently (worst case ~16.5s to ~7.5s, inside the concurrency group's 10s exit budget).

Two open questions were added: whether an endpoint's addresses should be tried with happy eyeballs (RFC 8305) instead of equal shares of one deadline, and whether a provider's locality should be a field on the discovery event rather than inferred from its machines' addresses.

Three more decisions were recorded: the sleep fence on errored provider snapshots lands at the consumer's ingress (with the audit of every clock read in the desktop client that motivated placing it there, and the heartbeat race all four fences share), the surfaces now receive an explicit "unmeasured" device condition rather than "fine", and the band's and card's running-restart exception is narrowed to the user's own bounce.
